key_insight: A passive, physics-based sloshing surrogate combines curved-meniscus effects, viscous losses and contact-line hysteresis to improve low-gravity tank predictions.
engineering_relevance: Faster-than-real-time coupled spacecraft–sloshing simulation can support control analysis while accounting for uncertain damping.
method: Port-Hamiltonian reduced-order model with curvature-corrected inertia and restoring forces.
Convex dissipation potential combining bulk, Stokes-layer and contact-line losses.
Analytical propagation between nonsmooth contact-line stick–slip events.
evidence_signal: Across 42 drop-tower and ground measurements, curvature correction reduced RMS frequency error from 24% to 4%; MODE force errors were 11–35% with calibrated hysteresis versus 149–208% for an ideal pinned line.
watch_item: Uncertain wetting and remaining response discrepancies warrant damping ranges rather than a single nominal value in spacecraft control analyses.
paper_title: A curvature-corrected port-Hamiltonian reduced-order model for dissipative sloshing with contact-line hysteresis in low-gravity tanks
